data.body:
**STOPPING THE LOOP ON A REAL FINDING: the code-review gate NEVER honours per-step model declarations. 3768 must NOT close, and 172e (CLOSED) shipped the same latent gap.**

Evidence: a real `rebar review-code` run with `REBAR_USAGE_LOG` (one JSON record per LLM call) under an INVERTED class config (frontier=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-8, standard=anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6). NINE calls, ALL `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` — including `code-review-verify`, whose `model: standard` was landed by 172e and is not my change. Under that config verify MUST have been sonnet. So the gate ignores step-level classes entirely; my 3768 YAML is correct in form but INERT, as is 172e's.

Ruled out, each separately: the package loads MY worktree gate with all five declarations; `code_review/shim.py:119 review_code` really executes the gate via `produce_code_review_verdict`; the config pointer IS honoured (`resolve_class('frontier')` -> bedrock, with and without repo_root); and `resolve_model(cfg, step='frontier')` -> bedrock while `step=None` -> the bare default, which is exactly what was logged.

WHY MY 9 TESTS AND 6/6 MUTATIONS MISSED IT — the post-mortem that matters. Every test asserted either YAML content or `resolve_model_string(<token>)` in isolation; none asserted that the ENGINE PASSES the token to the resolver during a run. So every mutation I could devise perturbed the YAML or the class table and was duly caught, while none could distinguish 'declaration honoured' from 'declaration ignored'. The plan's own text demanded a RUNTIME assertion and I did not write one. A green suite plus biting mutations is not evidence of behaviour if nothing observes the behaviour.

THREE PROBES IN A ROW WOULD HAVE MISLED ME, and the discrimination discipline is what saved it: (1) the caching-warning grep captured 3 of 9 calls, so I announced then retracted a conclusion drawn from a biased sample; (2) a non-inverted config predicts the same observation whether the class works or not; (3) 'config not loaded' predicts it too, and had to be eliminated on its own. Only the inverted config plus the per-call log is decisive.

OPERATOR DECISIONS NEEDED — I am not taking these unilaterally: (a) expand 3768 to include the gate plumbing fix (its Problem section's premise 'code review is only PARTLY split' is now falsified — there is NO split at runtime), or carry the fix as a new ticket; (b) 172e is CLOSED with a criterion ('the three verifier paths resolve the standard class') that was satisfied by unit tests over helpers rather than an observed runtime binding — that likely warrants a follow-up, which I have not filed.

STATE: 11 closed (7761, 172e, 343b, 7cbe, b00f, d8ef, b300, b5fe, d23e, epic 9227, eb58). Gerrit 1164 (d23e) and 1169 (3768) are both +1/+1 and submittable, NOTHING submitted. 3768 is CLAIMED and in_progress with the defect recorded on it. 0d76/eb6e/8625 remain blocked by 3768; 5e75 is ready.
